No actual crossing or genericity premise is needed for this algebraic identity, but such geometry is derived in its source-facing use.

If chi is continuous at the actual centre and its centre value is nonzero, chi(curve(t))*chi(centre) is strictly positive on a neighbourhood of the actual interval-subtype zero. On the minimum of this radius and the source F sign-change radius, substituting F=psi*chi is legitimate because both factors are nonzero. Regrouping the two-side product shows the psi product must be negative because the factor product is positive. This preserves the exact SignChanges predicate and its valid germ-domain radius; no supplied same-sign neighbourhood is assumed.
